mechanism_narrative: A sustained growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic expansion, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive (relative to the 3-year rolling average).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong labor market conditions and consumer spending, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and RSAFS does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE falls and RSAFS rises.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the economy is in a contraction phase, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which typically lead to higher interest rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL is rising (relative to the 3-year rolling average).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS indicates an active monetary tightening cycle, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are rising.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising housing starts (HOUST > 1900 thousand units), the housing sector expansion boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST > 1900.
